questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road widens ahead.
Lane reduction; the right lane ends soon.
Highway entrance ramp ahead.
Lane reduction; the left lane ends soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane reduction; the right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to check if someone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

questions.question: What is the only way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to reduce your BAC is to wait for your body to process the alcohol over time. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not lower your BAC or reduce alcohol's effects. They may keep you awake, but they cannot make you sober.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing the street in a crosswalk. You must:

options.text: Honk your horn to alert them to your presence.
Slow down and move around the pedestrian at a slow pace.
Stop until the pedestrian is out of the crosswalk.
Accelerate as soon as the pedestrian has moved past your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the pedestrian is out of the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks. Do not make a pedestrian wait for you. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not put too much thought into it because all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Disregard any obvious defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes before driving to familiarize yourself with the operation and location of all the vehicle's equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes before driving to familiarize yourself with the operation and location of all the vehicle's equipment.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to learn where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of concentration.
Poor coordination.
Slower judgment.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: You are driving on the roadway and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, move to the right side of the road and stop. Slow down and let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic and cannot move right away, drive slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. You should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.
Stop and back up.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a shoulder or freeway is illegal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Multiple turns.
Lane shifting.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic.
questions.explanation: This warning sign alerts you that traffic from the right will be merging. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Honk at the officer.
Check to see what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Instead, go to the next exit and safely turn around there.

questions.question: What is the danger of driving much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: It makes you a very safe driver.
It always gives you the right-of-way.
Other cars should not be allowed to pass you.
It may create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road must do what?

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is possible to do so.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the roadway, what should you do?

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you entered the wrong freeway ramp.
Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, go to the next exit instead of backing up.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never try to go around the gate.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger directs you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red signals and gates are operating.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: When turning right from a two-way street onto another two-way street, what should you do?

options.text: Signal your intention to turn for at least 100 feet.
Look out the right side of the windshield for pedestrians.
Get into the right lane well ahead of the turn.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Get into the right lane and signal well before you turn. Watch for pedestrians crossing the intersection by looking out the right side of your windshield.

questions.question: What provides the best protection in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts can double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags used with safety belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Always wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: What is important when driving on major highways?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. Avoid looking at one thing for more than a few seconds to prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum safe speed for exiting a highway. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.
